re_line: Fifth Plenum purge & Zhang Shengmin's Politburo rise · Nvidia-Huang spy claims · PLA naval buildup · BYD profit miss
morning_memo: Beijing's Fifth Plenum communique locks in tighter party discipline and confirms the expulsion of 33 senior officials, including former diplomat Liu Jianchao.
Zhang Shengmin, the general who ran the PLA's internal anti-corruption purge, is elevated to the Politburo as CMC vice chairman.
WSJ and NYT report a Chinese executive close to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is suspected by US intelligence of relaying information to Beijing; MOFA calls the report 'groundless speculation.'

key_stat.label: SSE Composite decline today despite AI-sector strength
key_stat.context: Chinese investors rotated into long-bond ETFs and Hong Kong outflows accelerated even as chip and AI earnings held up, per Bloomberg and CNN coverage of the divergence.

prc_government.official: PBOC statement (no individual spokesperson named in source)
prc_government.action: Shifts to daily overnight reverse repo auctions
prc_government.document: Notice on daily overnight reverse repo tenders from Nov 2
prc_government.detail: The PBOC will conduct overnight reverse repo tenders every business day starting *Nov 2*, with 7-day operations reserved for tax periods and month-end, as it moves toward using the overnight rate as its main policy rate.

prc_government.action: Issues notice to further liberalize Hainan Free Trade Port trade rules
prc_government.document: Notice on further raising Hainan Free Trade Port trade liberalization and facilitation levels
prc_government.detail: MOFCOM and three other departments jointly issued a notice aimed at raising trade liberalization and facilitation standards in the Hainan Free Trade Port.
prc_government.source_label: MOFCOM / 中国贸易救济信息网

prc_government.action: Southern Theater Command patrols near Scarborough Shoal
prc_government.detail: PLA Southern Theater Command forces conducted a combat-readiness patrol in the territorial waters and airspace around Huangyan Dao (Scarborough Shoal); China Coast Guard ran a parallel law-enforcement patrol in the same area.

prc_government.action: Reports continued implementation of 10 cross-strait measures
prc_government.detail: **Chen Binhua** said Beijing continues expanding market access for Taiwanese agricultural and fishery goods, including pomelo and sugar-apple sales on the mainland, under the April 12 ten-point package.

prc_government.action: Holds third China-Sweden green transition investment working group meeting
prc_government.detail: MOFCOM convened the third session of the bilateral China-Sweden green transition investment working group in Sweden, continuing the clean-energy investment cooperation mechanism.

npc_politburo.action: Releases communique incorporating Xi Jinping Thought on Party Building
npc_politburo.detail: The communique frames 'full and rigorous Party self-governance' as an integrated system to control members, supervise officials and implement decisions, per Sinocism; study campaigns on the Plenum and the 21st Party Congress are expected to follow.

**Zhang Shengmin**, CMC vice chairman who led the military's anti-corruption purge, was appointed to the Politburo as the party tightens discipline, per FT. The appointment follows the Oct 2025 expulsion of former CMC vice chairmen He Weidong and Miao Hua.

npc_politburo.action: Communique vows officials will have no 'audacity, opportunity, or desire to commit corruption'
npc_politburo.detail: The plenum communique highlighted 'unwritten rules' as a key issue to address, per SCMP, as Xi renewed a years-long anti-corruption drive.

npc_politburo.action: Plenum sees record expulsions and attendance absences
npc_politburo.detail: Reuters reported the conclave on toughening party discipline saw record-low attendance alongside the surprise Politburo appointment and the record expulsions.

calendar_watch.headline: US midterm elections
calendar_watch.detail: Control of Congress at stake; House Select Committee on the CCP composition could shift depending on outcome.

calendar_watch.headline: Busan-deal suspensions approach lapse
calendar_watch.detail: The one-year suspensions of the BIS Affiliates Rule and China's Oct 2025 rare-earth export controls are due to expire around this date unless extended.

calendar_watch.headline: PLAAF 77th anniversary tied to 16th Zhuhai Airshow
calendar_watch.detail: MND says activities will be organized around the theme 'tracing roots, building dreams' linked to the China Airshow.

calendar_watch.headline: APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting, Shenzhen
calendar_watch.detail: China hosts; Trump attendance and any Trump-Xi meeting on the margins remain unconfirmed.

calendar_watch.headline: Taiwan nine-in-one local elections
calendar_watch.detail: 22 mayors and magistrates and roughly 11,000 offices up for election, read as a mid-term referendum on President Lai.

overnight_items.headline: Hong Kong Leader Apologises for Deadly Tai Po Fire, Pledges Reform
overnight_items.body_text: Chief Executive **John Lee** apologized for the deadly Tai Po apartment fire and announced his housing secretary would step down after an inquiry found departments had overlooked fire hazards. Lee defended the government's broader handling even as he pledged reform.

overnight_items.headline: Cathay Pacific Says 53,000 Bookings Compromised in Amadeus Cyberattack
overnight_items.body_text: **Cathay Pacific** revealed personal data and flight details from *53,000* bookings were exposed after hackers breached technology provider Amadeus IT Group, which serves hundreds of airlines worldwide. The unauthorized access occurred between August 2023 and September 2026.

overnight_items.headline: Inside the Breakdown of Trump's $1.5 Trillion Pentagon Plan
overnight_items.body_text: The Washington Post examines internal strains in the administration's $1.5 trillion Pentagon spending plan. Further detail on China-specific force-posture implications was not available in the published summary.

overnight_items.headline: Chinese Junk Dollar Bonds Head for Worst Week in a Year on Huafa
overnight_items.body_text: Chinese high-yield dollar bonds are on track for their worst week in a year, Bloomberg reported, driven by stress around developer **Huafa**. The selloff points to renewed strain in property-linked credit.

overnight_items.headline: China's Oil Majors Get More Firepower for Energy Security Push
overnight_items.body_text: Bloomberg reports Chinese state oil majors are getting additional capital and policy support as part of Beijing's energy-security drive. The push coincides with China building gas and fuel buffers ahead of winter.

overnight_items.headline: Earnings Give European Auto Stocks Respite as China Reshapes Industry
overnight_items.body_text: European automakers' latest earnings offered brief investor relief even as Chinese competition continues to reshape the global auto industry, Reuters reported. The respite comes alongside Volkswagen's widened Q3 operating loss.

overnight_items.headline: China's Homegrown Cosmetics Contenders Face Battle to Glow Up
overnight_items.body_text: FT profiles Chinese beauty brands **Yatsen** and Proya as they push into cosmetics markets still dominated by foreign incumbents. Domestic competition and thin margins complicate the overseas expansion.

overnight_items.headline: Malaysia Becomes Crossroads of US-China AI Data Center Boom
overnight_items.body_text: US and Chinese tech giants are pouring billions into Malaysian data centers, straining local power and water resources while testing the limits of Washington's chip-export restrictions, per NYT. The buildout underscores Southeast Asia's role as an AI-infrastructure workaround hub.

us_china.headline: FCC Votes to Ban All Chinese Labs From Testing US Electronics
us_china.body_text: The FCC voted to bar Chinese laboratories from certifying US electronics for sale, closing what it called a national-security loophole. The move follows a string of 2026 actions restricting Chinese firms' access to the US telecom and device-testing supply chain.

us_china.headline: US Plans to Ban Chinese Telecom Firms From Direct Access to US Phone Numbers
us_china.body_text: Washington is preparing to bar Chinese telecom carriers from directly obtaining US phone numbers, part of a broader push to limit PRC firms' access to US communications infrastructure. The move lands the same week as the FCC testing-lab ban and the new BGI genomics import ban.

us_china.headline: US Bans Imports From Three Chinese Genomics Firms Over Xinjiang Forced Labor
us_china.body_text: DHS added **BGI Genomics**, MGI Tech and Shenzhen BGI Technology to the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act Entity List, saying they 'helped collect genetic material used to track persecuted ethnic minorities.' MOFCOM called the ban baseless and vowed countermeasures.

us_china.headline: US Army Pacific Prepares for Possible 2027 Taiwan Conflict
us_china.body_text: USARPAC commander Gen. **Ronald Clark** said the 'Davidson window', the timeframe for possible Chinese military action against Taiwan, remains valid, and the Army is rotating forces and equipment west of the International Date Line under its 'Army Ready Forward' initiative. The window traces to a 2021 warning by then-INDOPACOM chief Adm. Philip Davidson.

us_china.headline: Palantir's Gallagher Warns AI Race Raises Taiwan Invasion Stakes
us_china.body_text: Palantir defense head **Mike Gallagher** said advances in AI make 'the logic of Xi Jinping sacrificing enormously to take Taiwan... more compelling,' citing TSMC's chokepoint role. Chinese embassy spokesman Liu Chang said 'the Taiwan question is China's internal affair' and urged the US to 'act prudently.'

china_world.headline: Pakistan's 24-Hour Reversal on Taiwan Airline Overflight Ban Fuels Squeeze Fears
china_world.body_text: Pakistan briefly barred Taiwan's China Airlines and EVA Air from its airspace citing its 'one China policy' before restoring overflight permits hours later, through Mar 27, 2027. At least 12 China Airlines Europe-bound flights had already rerouted over Russia to avoid the airspace.

china_world.headline: Analysts: PLA Warship Activity Signals Integrated First Island Chain Operations
china_world.body_text: Tamkang University's **Lin Ying-yu** said PLA naval movements from the northern, eastern and southern theater commands reflect a unified 'First Island Chain theater' rather than separate drills, citing the Liaoning carrier group's passage through the Miyako Strait toward the Philippine Sea. He added that focus on the carrier 'should not overshadow' the Type 055 destroyer's presence.

china_world.headline: Philippines-China Tensions Resurface at Close of ASEAN Defence Gathering
china_world.body_text: Beijing accused a Philippine politician of obstructing its participation in the ASEAN defence ministers' gathering in Cebu on Oct 29, where US Defense Secretary **Pete Hegseth** attended in person while China sent only a defense attache. The spat follows months of friction over South China Sea maritime disputes.

china_world.headline: China Conducts Combat-Readiness Patrols Around Scarborough Shoal
china_world.body_text: China's Southern Theater Command and coast guard conducted 'combat readiness patrols' around Scarborough Shoal, calling them a 'necessary countermeasure' to Philippine 'rights-violation and provocative acts.' The patrol coincides with heightened PLA naval activity across the First Island Chain.

china_world.headline: Retired Taiwan Navy Ship Donated to Philippines Amid ASEAN Rift
china_world.body_text: Taiwan transferred its retired Kinmen-class patrol vessel to the Philippine Coast Guard via a civilian organization, drawing disputes over usage limits and fishing rights. The donation coincided with Beijing's downgraded ASEAN defence-meeting attendance versus the in-person appearance by the US defense chief.

china_world.headline: Japanese Spy Drama 'Vivant' Draws Beijing's Ire
china_world.body_text: Chinese state media has intensified criticism of 'Vivant,' a Japanese thriller featuring Chinese spies, with the show's creators defending it as 'completely fictional,' per NYT. The backlash follows weeks of tension between Beijing and Tokyo over Prime Minister **Sanae Takaichi**'s security posture.

china_world.headline: Chinese EVs Gain Ground in South Korea, Struggle in Japan
china_world.body_text: Chinese electric-vehicle makers are winning converts in South Korea even as they face a 'rougher road' in Japan's more protected auto market, Reuters reported. The divergence highlights differing regulatory and consumer barriers across Northeast Asia.

china_world.headline: Xi Holds Welcome Ceremony for German President Steinmeier
china_world.body_text: **Xi Jinping** held a welcome ceremony in Beijing on Oct 30 for German President Steinmeier's state visit, per Xinhua. The visit comes the same week Xi hosted Switzerland's federal president for a cooperation-document signing.

china_world.headline: Saint Lucia PM Seeks Deeper Taiwan Ties on Five-Day State Visit
china_world.body_text: Saint Lucian Prime Minister **Philip Pierre** met President Lai Ching-te in Taipei and called for expanded scholarships and a new cultural center, citing *19 years* of bilateral friendship. More than 400 young people from Saint Lucia have studied in Taiwan under existing programs.

top_stories.headline: Beijing Confirms Record Expulsion of 33 Officials as Xi's Purge Deepens
top_stories.body: China's Communist Party confirmed the expulsion of *33* senior officials, including former senior diplomat **Liu Jianchao** and ex-**Xi Jinping** military secretary Zhong Shaojun, at the close of the Fifth Plenum. Many of those named had been missing from public view for months or longer without official explanation, the New York Times reported.

top_stories.headline: Chinese Executive Close to Nvidia's Jensen Huang Suspected of Giving China Information
top_stories.body: US intelligence concluded a Chinese executive tied to Singapore-based data-center firm Megaspeed developed a close relationship with **Jensen Huang** and may have relayed insight on US AI policy to Beijing, per WSJ and NYT. **Trump** was briefed roughly a year ago and chose not to act; MOFA spokesman Guo Jiakun called the report 'groundless speculation' and 'an attempt to smear China.'

top_stories.headline: Taiwan NSC Chief Maps 53 Chinese Vessels Spanning Japan to the Philippines
top_stories.body: NSC Secretary-General **Joseph Wu** posted a map showing *53* Chinese naval and coast guard vessels, 34 of them warships, including the carrier Liaoning, stretching from southern Japan to Taiwan and off the Philippines. 'The simultaneous threat to Taiwan, Japan and the Philippines is obvious,' Wu said.

top_stories.headline: BYD Profit Growth Slows as Export-Led Recovery Loses Steam
top_stories.body: **BYD**'s Q3 net profit rose roughly *28 percent* year-on-year per Nikkei, but missed analyst estimates as the automaker's export surge failed to fully offset weakening domestic demand. FT called the overseas expansion's rising importance a response to 'roadblocks in domestic market.'
top_stories.src_line: Bloomberg / Reuters / FT / Nikkei Asia, Oct 29 2026

top_stories.headline: China-Switzerland Trade Deal Signed as Xi Hosts Swiss President
top_stories.body: **Xi Jinping** met Switzerland's federal president in Beijing as the two countries signed a cooperation document, bucking the broader trend toward protectionism, per Reuters. The agreement follows Beijing's parallel courting of European leaders this week, including a welcome ceremony for German President Steinmeier.

also_today.headline: Chinese Startup Uses AI Lasers to Target Mosquitoes
also_today.body_text: A Chinese startup claims its AI-and-laser system can track and destroy mosquitoes while avoiding people and pets, using sensors developed for self-driving cars, per NYT.

also_today.headline: Beijing Moves to Curb China's City-Ranking Obsession
also_today.body_text: The Economist reports Chinese authorities are moving to discourage the popular practice of ranking cities by GDP and other metrics.

also_today.headline: China's Transport-Infrastructure Investment Has Peaked
also_today.body_text: The Economist finds China's decades-long transport-infrastructure buildout has passed its peak as the economy shifts toward services and high-tech manufacturing.

also_today.headline: Hong Kong's Push to Make the Yuan Part of Everyday Life
also_today.body_text: SCMP examines Hong Kong's drive to expand yuan use in retail payments, government spending and cross-border trade under Chief Executive John Lee's latest five-year plan.

also_today.headline: China's Gallium-Nitride Chipmakers Chase AI Data-Center Demand
also_today.body_text: Guancha reports China's GaN power-semiconductor makers are pivoting from saturated fast-charger markets toward automotive and AI-server power supplies as margins compress.

also_today.source: 美国之音中文 (VOA Chinese ZH)
also_today.headline: Taiwan Watches US Midterms for Signs of Shifting Support
also_today.body_text: VOA Chinese reports Taiwan officials are watching the Nov 3 US midterm elections closely, questioning whether cross-party support for the island will translate into concrete policy.

also_today.headline: Chinese Scholar Zhu Feng: 'Kissinger's Era Has Passed'
also_today.body_text: Nanjing University's Zhu Feng argues in a China-US intergenerational dialogue that Kissinger's era is over and his diplomatic legacy needs reinterpreting, per The Paper.

business_economy.headline: PAG Agrees to Buy Evergrande Property Unit for $513 Million
business_economy.body_text: Hong Kong-based private equity firm **PAG** offered *$513 million* to liquidators of China Evergrande's property-services arm, which FT called 'a rare win for creditors' of the world's most indebted developer. The deal gives PAG a 51 percent stake, per Bloomberg and Nikkei.

business_economy.headline: China Set to Lose LNG Import Crown to Japan on Weak Demand
business_economy.body_text: Weak domestic gas demand is set to push China behind Japan as the world's top LNG importer, Reuters reported, as Beijing builds gas-storage buffers ahead of winter.

business_economy.headline: Hong Kong Stocks Lose a Key Backer as Chinese Investors Head for Exit
business_economy.body_text: Mainland Chinese investors are pulling back from Hong Kong equities, removing a major source of support for the market, Bloomberg reported, alongside today's *2.66 percent* SSE Composite decline.

business_economy.headline: Chinese Investors Seek Shelter in Long-Bond ETFs as Stocks Sink
business_economy.body_text: Domestic investors are rotating into long-dated government bond ETFs as mainland equities slide, Bloomberg reported, even as the Hang Seng gained 0.87 percent today.

business_economy.headline: China's AI and Tech Boom Isn't Saving Its Stock Markets
business_economy.body_text: CNN reports the global AI boom sustaining China's economic momentum this year has failed to offset 'domestic woes, particularly in its stock market,' highlighting a gap between tech-sector strength and macro sentiment.

business_economy.headline: Toyota, Honda, Nissan Slash China Output as Gasoline Car Market Shrinks
business_economy.body_text: Japanese automakers continue cutting China production as demand for gasoline vehicles fades and intelligent-EV technology from domestic rivals advances, Nikkei reported.

business_economy.headline: China Upends Global Drug Development With Cheap, Rapid Human Trials
business_economy.body_text: China's low-cost, fast-turnaround clinical-trial infrastructure is drawing Western drugmakers including Roche, AstraZeneca and Novartis, Bloomberg reported, raising questions for regulators about trial-data provenance.

official_line.speaker: Liu Chang
official_line.topic: Palantir warning on AI and a possible Chinese move on Taiwan
official_line.statement: The Taiwan question is China's internal affair. Stronger cooperation between enterprises on both sides of the Taiwan Strait in semiconductors and other fields is the right path toward mutual benefit and win-win outcomes.
official_line.context: Response to Palantir defense head Mike Gallagher's remarks that AI-driven competition makes a Chinese move on Taiwan 'more compelling.'

official_line.topic: Taiwan defense ministry inviting the US to observe military exercises
official_line.statement: Attempting to 'seek independence by relying on external forces' is a dead end.
official_line.original_zh: 妄图“倚外谋独”是死路一条
official_line.context: Response to Taiwan's defense ministry inviting US observers to planned military exercises.

personnel_changes.name: Zhang Shengmin
personnel_changes.detail: Appointed to the Politburo after leading the PLA's internal anti-corruption purge as CMC vice chairman; follows the Oct 2025 expulsion of predecessors He Weidong and Miao Hua.

personnel_changes.name: Liu Jianchao
personnel_changes.detail: Confirmed expelled from the party at the close of the Fifth Plenum after not being seen publicly since Jul 2025; NYT describes him as a 'prominent former diplomat.'

personnel_changes.name: Zhong Shaojun

xinhua_delta.last_appearance_note: Tracker flagged a 55-day absence, but today's PLA Daily and CGTN items confirm Xi Jinping held a welcome ceremony for German President Steinmeier, met Switzerland's federal president for a cooperation-document signing, and chaired a CPC Central Committee symposium with non-party figures in Beijing on Oct 30 — superseding the prior absence flag.
